result.reasoning:
The only part of the finding that survives is the uncontested code fact: `cross_age` (ops_ext.py:703-713) returns `t + 10000` for every name finite on row 0, so those names tie on any given day. Every distinctive, number-changing claim built on top of that is wrong, and the suggested fix would break the book.

1) "并列块一模一样(93%)" is false. The 92.912% the finding quotes is anatomy's `上市:250日以上`, which scripts/anatomy.py:124 defines as `old_name OR cumsum(isfinite) >= 250` — that is cross_valid_count's saturated block, a strict superset of cross_age's row-0 block. The row-0 block can be bounded from the stored numbers alone: `上市:不足250日` = 7.08825% of utrain stock-days, that mask can only contain post-view-start listings, and each such name supplies at most 250 young stock-days in a 1359-day window, so post-start names >= 96.3/250 = 38.5% of the average universe and the row-0 tie block is <= 61.5%, never 93%. On a cadence-calibrated panel (1942 days = len(fuse_s2.json['dates']), 3485 row-0 names + 2169 IPOs at real yearly A-share counts; it reproduces `上市:不足250日` = 7.222% vs the stored 7.088%) the last utrain day has a cross_age tie block of 65.5% against cross_valid_count's 93.8%, and cross_age ranks 1509 further names (28.3% of the universe) with 767 distinct values. So the docstring sentence the finding wants deleted — "Unlike cross_valid_count it does not saturate at the window" — is true and load-bearing, and the 10000 convention is already stated in the sentence immediately before it.

2) "剔掉的是同一批" is false, and the project's own stored run proves it without any synthetic panel. h_K_ex_new and h3_K_ex_age_cont share y = neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30)) and both got hl=0.0, so identical daily cuts would give bit-identical panels. They do not: utrain 16.672526%/2.5061/turnover 0.029342 vs 17.213279%/2.5281/turnover 0.028628, valid 24.61% vs 26.32%, and the long book's share of `上市:不足250日` is 0.37670% vs 0.00000% (anatomy_s3.json). On my calibrated panel the two bands intersect in only 429 of 1065 names on the last utrain day.

3) The finding's reproduction only works because its panel contradicts the data it was calibrated against: 7.088% is a stock-day share, not a name share. The reporter's 700x1000 panel yields `上市:不足250日` = 1.314% under anatomy's own definition (5.4x too few young stock-days) and has no young name at all in its first 460 rows. That is what forces the band entirely into the tie block and makes the two screens coincide.

4) The suggested fix is actively harmful, reproduced as written: `torch.isfinite(-inf)` is False, so both "old = -inf" and "old = NaN" drop every row-0 name out of `_lexi`'s `ok = isfinite(y) & isfinite(x)` mask. The screen's universe falls from 5324 to 1838 names, the long book from 533 to 184 with zero row-0 names in it, and the factor is no longer measured against A-shares — the 65% of the universe that is dropped also leaves the equal-weight benchmark.

5) The residual that is true is weaker and is not a cross_age defect. Because `_lexi`'s band is a 20% quota, the age band must dip into the row-0 block while post-start listings are fewer than 20% of the day's universe: on the calibrated panel the tied share of the band is 18.6pp of the universe in 2018, 14.2pp in 2019, 7.4pp in 2020, and exactly 0 from day 802 (~early 2021) onward for every later day — so the valid-segment reading (+26.32%) and anything on holdout are clean, and the utrain figure is contaminated only in its 2018-2020 portion, not by a fixed 12.9pp every day. That mechanism is the same reviewer's other finding (_pct_rank ordinal ranks + _lexi quota band, ops_ext.py:226), whose suggested_fix already lists h3_K_ex_age_cont among the rows to recompute. Rejecting this item therefore loses nothing actionable, while keeping it as filed would put a false equivalence ("cross_age == cross_valid_number, 93% tie") and a book-breaking fix into the handoff.

6) The trailing warning about recomputing on holdout only describes no existing code path: every PanelSet in partura/ and scripts/ is built on SPLITS["full"] and sliced afterwards (panels.py:414 split_slice), and scripts/idea_search.py uses 20180102-20230807 with the same warmup, so its row 0 is the same calendar day and cross_age is unchanged on the overlapping rows. No stored number is affected.

result.corrected_fix:
Do NOT apply the suggested encoding change. `old = -inf` and `old = NaN` are equivalent here (torch.isfinite(-inf) is False) and both delete every pre-data-start name from `_lexi`'s ok mask, i.e. from both the long book and the equal-weight benchmark (book 533 -> 184 names, none of them row-0 in the reproduction). Leave the `age + 10000` convention alone: without listing dates it is the only defensible encoding, and the "does not saturate" sentence is factually correct (767 distinct ages among names cross_valid_count cannot separate at all).

What is worth doing, in order:
1. Docstring precision only (no behaviour change), on ops_ext.py cross_age: keep "Unlike cross_valid_count it does not saturate at the window" and add one clause — "names already trading on the first row of the view are mutually indistinguishable (one shared value per day, ~60% of the production panel's universe), so a cross-sectional rank of this operator has one large tie block at the old end." Also keep the existing "must be computed on the warmed full view and sliced afterwards" expectation explicit, since the operator reads row 0; today every PanelSet (partura/runner.py:96, study_tools.py:61, scripts/*.py) already does this, so nothing needs recomputing for that reason.
2. The number-changing part is not in cross_age; it is the quota band. Fix it where the other finding puts it (ops_ext.py:224 `_pct_rank` ordinal ranks + ops_ext.py:318 `_lexi`'s `(rx > lo) & (rx <= hi)`): make the band a condition on x rather than a 20% quota — thr = nanquantile(x, hi) computed per day over the ok mask, band = x >= thr — so a tie block enters whole or not at all and the band width adapts (7% young means 7% excluded, not 20%). With that change h3_K_ex_age_cont becomes the clean test the hypothesis's `why` field asks for.
3. When that row is recomputed, report it per period rather than as one utrain figure: the arbitrary-cut contamination is concentrated in 2018 (~19pp of the universe), 2019 (~14pp) and 2020 (~7pp) and is exactly zero from roughly mid-2021 onward, so the valid reading (+26.32%) and any holdout reading are unaffected, and the 2018-2020 rows of F103's year table are the only ones whose interpretation changes.
